properties.name: Dangun — Founding of Korea
properties.summary: Hwanung, son of the Lord of Heaven, descended to Mount Baekdu. A bear and tiger wished to become human. Given garlic and mugwort in a cave for 100 days, only the bear persevered, becoming a woman. She married Hwanung and bore Dangun, who founded Gojoseon (Old Korea) in 2333 BCE.

properties.name: Gumiho — Nine-Tailed Fox
properties.summary: The gumiho is a fox that has lived a thousand years, gaining the ability to transform into a beautiful woman. Unlike Japanese kitsune, Korean gumiho are typically malevolent, consuming the livers or hearts of men. Some stories tell of gumiho who genuinely fall in love and seek to become fully human through restraint.

properties.name: Tale of Chunhyang
properties.summary: Chunhyang, the daughter of a gisaeng (courtesan), secretly married the nobleman's son Mongryong. When Mongryong left for Seoul, the corrupt governor Byeon Hakdo tried to force Chunhyang to be his concubine. She refused and was tortured. Mongryong returned as a secret royal inspector and saved her. Their love transcended class.

properties.name: Princess Pyeonggang and the Fool Ondal
properties.summary: The spirited princess cried so much that her father promised her to the village fool Ondal. She left the palace and married him, training him in martial arts and scholarship. Ondal became the nation's greatest general, proving that talent and love transcend social status. He died in battle defending the kingdom.

properties.name: Changsega — Korean Creation Epic
properties.summary: In the beginning, the giant Mireuk separated heaven and earth and placed four bronze pillars at the corners. He created the sun, moon, and stars from hanging lamps. A rival, Seokga, challenged him to a flower-growing contest. Seokga cheated, but won power over the human world, explaining why evil exists.
